title: Two Sum in a Sorted Array
statement: Given a non-decreasing integer array nums and an integer target, return the zero-based indices of two distinct elements whose sum equals target. Return the pair with the smaller index first. Exactly one valid pair exists.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
common_wrong_approaches: Returning values instead of indices
Using one index twice
Using a quadratic nested-loop search
Returning indices in the wrong order
grading_notes: Tests include negative numbers, duplicates, and solutions at array boundaries.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement: Given a string s, return the length of the longest contiguous substring containing no repeated characters. Treat characters as Python string code points and compare them exactly.
constraints: s may contain spaces, punctuation, digits, and Unicode characters
common_wrong_approaches: Resetting the whole window on every duplicate
Returning the substring instead of its length
Failing when the duplicate is before the current window
Assuming the input contains only lowercase English letters
grading_notes: Tests cover empty strings, all-unique strings, repeated characters, spaces, and Unicode.

title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
statement: Given a list of intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return the merged intervals sorted by start. Intervals that touch at an endpoint are considered overlapping (for example, [1,3] and [3,5] merge). Input intervals have start <= end.
common_wrong_approaches: Not sorting intervals first
Treating endpoint-touching intervals as separate
Mutating shared input lists in surprising ways
Failing on empty input or one interval
grading_notes: The output must be sorted and must not contain mergeable adjacent intervals.

title: Shortest Path in a Binary Grid
statement: Given an m by n grid of 0s and 1s, find the shortest path length from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell. A 0 is open and a 1 is blocked. You may move up, down, left, or right. Count cells in the path, including both endpoints. Return -1 if no path exists. If either endpoint is blocked, return -1.
output_format: int path length in cells, or -1
common_wrong_approaches: Using DFS and assuming the first path is shortest
Counting moves rather than cells
Forgetting blocked start or destination
Marking cells visited too late and enqueueing duplicates excessively
grading_notes: Uses four-direction movement only; diagonal movement is not allowed.

title: Range Sum Query – Immutable Array
statement: Given an integer array nums and a list of inclusive queries [left, right], return the sum of nums[left:right+1] for every query. The array is immutable during all queries.
output_format: list[int] of query sums in input order
common_wrong_approaches: Using right-exclusive indexing for an inclusive query
Recomputing every sum from scratch
Building prefix sums without a leading zero
Off-by-one errors for queries starting at index zero
grading_notes: Negative values are valid; Python integer arithmetic avoids fixed-width overflow.
